title: Study Shows How Earth’s Orbit Affects Ice Ages
titleZh: 研究表明地球轨道如何影响冰河时期
credits: Issam Ahmed wrote this story for Agence-France Presse. Andrew Smith adapted it for VOA Learning English.

sentences.en: A recent study suggests the next ice age will likely begin in about 11,000 years unless emissions change the effects of natural climate cycles.
sentences.zh: 最近一项研究表明，除非排放改变自然气候周期的影响，否则下一次冰河时代可能将在约11000年后开始。

sentences.en: An ice age is a period of reduced temperatures causing ice to cover large areas of the northern and southern parts of the world.
sentences.zh: 冰河时代是指气温降低、使冰层覆盖世界南北大片区域的时期。

sentences.en: A group of scientists studied changes in the shape of the Earth’s orbit around the sun, the tilt of the Earth’s axis and the movement of the axis itself, called a wobble.
sentences.zh: 一组科学家研究了地球绕太阳运行的轨道形状变化、地球自转轴的倾斜以及自转轴本身的运动，后者被称为“章动”。

sentences.en: These three motions are believed to happen in cycles.
sentences.zh: 这三种运动被认为以周期性方式发生。

sentences.en: The Serbian scientist Milutin Milankovitch developed a theory about 100 years ago that these cycles affected Earth’s long-term climate.
sentences.zh: 塞尔维亚科学家米卢廷·米兰科维奇大约100年前提出了一种理论，认为这些周期会影响地球的长期气候。

sentences.en: The team noted that small changes in Earth’s orbit around the Sun caused predictable cycles of warming and cooling over a period of about 100,000 years.
sentences.zh: 该团队指出，地球绕太阳运行轨道的微小变化会在约10万年的周期内引起可预测的升温与降温循环。

sentences.en: These findings permitted the team to determine how the three factors of tilt, wobble, and the shape of Earth's orbit might have affected the Earth’s climate over the last 900,000 years.
sentences.zh: 这些发现使该团队得以确定倾斜、章动和地球轨道形状这三个因素在过去90万年间如何影响地球气候。

sentences.en: The group published its findings in Science on February 27.
sentences.zh: 该小组于2月27日在《科学》杂志上发表了其研究成果。

sentences.en: The scientists examined a million-year record of climate by looking at ice sheets across the northern half of the world and deep ocean temperatures.
sentences.zh: 科学家通过观察北半球冰盖和深海温度，研究了一百万年的气候记录。

sentences.en: They then compared this data with small but regular changes in Earth’s orbit over time.
sentences.zh: 随后，他们将这一数据与地球轨道随时间发生的微小但规律的变化进行了比较。

sentences.en: The lead writer of the study is Stephen Barker, a professor at Cardiff University in Britain.
sentences.zh: 该研究的主要作者是英国卡迪夫大学教授斯蒂芬·巴克。

sentences.en: He told the French News Agency (AFP) that for many years it has been difficult for scientists to show exactly how small changes in Earth’s orbit have led to huge changes between warm and cold periods.
sentences.zh: 他向法国新闻社（法新社）表示，多年来，科学家一直难以确切证明地球轨道的微小变化如何导致冷暖时期之间的巨大变化。

sentences.en: Earth is believed to go through cycles of ice ages and warm periods.
sentences.zh: 人们认为地球会经历冰河时代与温暖时期的循环。

sentences.en: The last ice age is thought to have ended around 11,700 years ago.
sentences.zh: 上一次冰河时代被认为大约在11700年前结束。

sentences.en: Scientists, such as Milankovitch, have long seen a connection between Earth's orbit and climate.
sentences.zh: 像米兰科维奇这样的科学家长期以来一直认为地球轨道与气候之间存在联系。

sentences.en: However, researchers have struggled to precisely date when each of the climate changes happened.
sentences.zh: 然而，研究人员一直难以精确确定每一次气候变化发生的时间。

sentences.en: It has also been difficult for them to know exactly which orbit positions affect the start and stop of cold or warm periods.
sentences.zh: 他们同样难以确切知道究竟是哪些轨道位置影响了寒冷或温暖时期的开始与结束。

sentences.en: Barker said his team of researchers studied slow changes in temperature over long periods of time instead of only looking at shorter periods of change between cold and warm climates.
sentences.zh: 巴克表示，他的研究小组研究的是长时间内温度的缓慢变化，而不是仅仅关注寒冷与温暖气候之间较短时期的变化。

sentences.en: Barker told AFP, "We would expect a glaciation to occur within the next 11,000 years, and it would end in 66,000 years' time."
sentences.zh: 巴克对法新社表示：“我们预计冰盖将在未来11000年内出现，并在66000年后结束。”

sentences.en: Lorraine Lisiecki is a professor at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and a co-writer of the study.
sentences.zh: 洛琳·莉斯基是加州大学圣巴巴拉分校的教授，也是该研究的共同作者。

sentences.en: She said the study shows that changes in climate over tens of thousands of years are not random.
sentences.zh: 她说，这项研究表明，气候在数万年间的变化并非随机。

sentences.en: The team aims to expand its findings to investigate the long-term effects of human activity on climate.
sentences.zh: 该团队希望将研究结果扩展开来，深入探究人类活动对气候的长期影响。

sentences.en: They also want to find out how it might affect Earth’s natural climate cycles.
sentences.zh: 他们还希望弄清这可能如何影响地球的自然气候周期。

sentences.en: I’m Andrew Smith.
sentences.zh: 我是安德鲁·史密斯。

glossary.def: the imaginary line around which the Earth revolves, or turns
glossary.zh: 地轴 (n.): 地球旋转的假想轴；自转轴

glossary.def: an action or set of actions that repeat over a regular period
glossary.zh: 循环 (n.): 周期性重复的动作；周期

glossary.def: a flat, wide extent of a material such as paper or ice
glossary.zh: 片 (n.): 平坦宽广的一片；薄片

glossary.def: something that affects a process or development
glossary.zh: 因素 (n.): 影响过程或发展的要素
摆动 (n.): 不稳的左右晃动

glossary.def: a period in which large areas of ice form and move
glossary.zh: 冰期 (n.): 大面积冰层形成移动的时期

glossary.def: showing no particular order or period
glossary.zh: 随机的 (adj.): 无特定顺序；无规律
